diagnosis.conclusion: Confirmed incomplete Argon CLI turns hitting local deadlines, compounded by CLI timeout/exit latency and unequal process-lifecycle handling. The retained evidence does not identify a terminal provider rate limit or account block, and does not prove a permanent provider hang. No single upstream cause of the long turns is established.
diagnosis.confidence: High for timeout and lifecycle mechanics; limited for why generation/file-tool turns are slow.

facts: Both relays pass --print-timeout 10m; their default external process budget is 660 seconds.
Candidate returncode 124 is synthesized by subprocess.TimeoutExpired; it is not a provider status or native agy exit code.
Argon metadata timed_out=true is synthesized at the Python 660-second deadline; returncode:null does not mean the process was never started.
CLI print timeout is an in-progress-turn deadline that may emit partial text; a warning is not a complete answer or an exit guarantee.

provider_hang.status: permanent hang unproven; long/incomplete turns observed
facts: Candidate PID 1151468 maps directly to cli-20261030_171930.log: startup 17:19:31, prompt forwarded 17:19:35, streamGenerateContent response IDs at 17:25:24, 17:25:32 and 17:28:53, print warning 17:30:14, shutdown starts 17:30:27, external reaping 17:30:29 UTC.
That call had a substantial generation delay, but generated multiple response IDs and advanced its CLI polling (978 polls, printed=18). These counters are not proof of a completed answer.
Configuration refreshes also log context deadline exceeded; those are separate requests and do not prove that generation itself returned a deadline error.
An already-running field retry later validated after 228.949 seconds without any diagnostic intervention.

lifecycle.status: confirmed contributor; separate from upstream slowness
facts: Candidate cli_transport starts a new session, retains Popen, waits up to 660 seconds, then kills its owned group and reaps the parent in finally. Every recorded candidate process sidecar is reaped. This is not a detach/nohup launch-acknowledgement pattern.

The older candidate _0003 attempt1 exited -9 before the full 660-second window (about 438 seconds reservation-to-finish). SIGKILL is established; its sender and cause are not established by the sidecar. Do not infer OOM, host timeout, or provider rejection from -9 alone.

Argon imports scripts/adjudicate.py run_transport. It retains a process and polls strict answer validation, but kills/terminates only the immediate Popen process, without start_new_session or owned descendant-group cleanup. Descendant survival is a code-level risk, not proof of an observed orphan.

The later successful Argon retry has returncode -9 with closed_after_valid_answer=true and validated=true. The helper itself terminates then kills a still-live CLI after strict final validation. This demonstrates valid-answer/CLI-exit divergence.
Candidate has no equivalent validated-answer early-close gate; adding one would have to use its own full strict validator, not heading or JSON presence alone.

native_ws1006.fact: Retained integration evidence records native harness WS1006/contextcancelled before complete output.
native_ws1006.interpretation: Abnormal WebSocket closure/context cancellation is transport-level evidence. It is not an HTTP 429, quota diagnosis, or proof that these later CLI calls have the same cause. Exact original native wire histories were not sufficiently linked here to establish the socket closer or a fixed host deadline.

bounded_longer_timeout_and_native_host_l.reason: Relay.run rejects max_calls with timeout>660, even though unbounded timeout accepts up to 900. Both CLI commands still hardcode print-timeout 10m. Increasing only the external wait cannot extend generation past the internal print deadline.
verified_host_facts: orchestratorMcp.ts declares timeoutMs for mode=wait only: default 10 minutes, waitTimedOut does not cancel the child. OrchestratorMcpService constants are DEFAULT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 and MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=3600000.

AcpSessionRuntime session/prompt awaits its retained active prompt fiber without a per-turn timeout at that seam; 90 seconds is session load, and 15 seconds is cancellation completion. These are not a maximum review runtime.
The observed candidate round used a Codex relay child, not a direct native Antigravity prompt. ACP prompt behavior does not certify the separate Codex command/tool runtime ceiling.
No fixed 12-minute or 15-minute delegated review runtime was established from the inspected code. Previous -9 and WS1006 events do not establish such a limit.
bounded_longer_timeout_and_native_host_l.verdict: A longer finite call is structurally possible in a retained native child lifecycle, because the 10-minute task wait is not a cancellation ceiling. It is NOT supported unchanged by the current bounded helper, and successful fit within the actual relay host execution budget is not yet certified.

conditional_budget_example_not_applied.explanation: Example only: 12 minutes generation, two minutes startup/exit allowance inside outer wait, plus three minutes outside for preparation/hash checks/cleanup/result publication. Host command/tool budget must cover the full bound; if it does not, do not run. These values do not assert that 12 minutes solves the slow turn.

required_before_real_execution: Verify the actual retained host command/tool deadline and startup/cleanup allowance with a local no-network synthetic subprocess; do not interpret a task_status wait timeout as child cancellation.
Make inner print timeout and outer deadline explicit and consistent in the proposed code, and deliberately revise the bounded guard only once host fit is established.
Run one wave per retained native execution; await all owned processes, finish cleanup, publish a terminal result, and return it before ending the relay turn. No detach/nohup or launch-only reply.

safe_proposed_fix.status: proposal only; no code or configuration changed
steps: Preserve Gemini 4 Argon (High), included-subscription consumer route, sandbox/read-only permissions, immutable prompts/inputs/raw histories and spent-attempt accounting. Preserve candidate circuit until parent explicitly authorizes any new execution.

First improve local transport observability: per-attempt private --log-file path, launch PID/session/group, monotonic launch/deadline/first-output/final-validation/exit/reap timestamps, and separate CLI-warning versus outer-timeout classification. Do not log credentials or account identifiers.
Make Argon cleanup use an owned session/process group like the candidate helper, including descendant cleanup on normal exit, timeout and interruption. Never signal unrelated/global agy processes.
Use each lane strict full-result validator for any validated-answer early-close path; require stable complete output and keep raw immutable. Never treat ## Answer alone or truncated JSON as success.

Use local fake subprocess fixtures to check delayed startup, truncated output, valid answer with hung exit, timeout, and owned descendant cleanup without a provider call. No real-review replay is needed to verify lifecycle mechanics.

Only after the host-budget prerequisite is established, propose a coordinated finite inner/outer timeout increase and single-wave execution for separately authorized remaining-budget work. Do not resume exhausted attempts, reset circuits automatically, refund uncertain reservations, or silently change the model.
safe_proposed_fix.upstream_fix_limit: No confirmed provider-side hang, quota problem, or credential defect can be repaired from these retained logs alone. A timeout increase may permit a slow turn to complete; it cannot be represented as a demonstrated cure.
